injectionLagP95Ms.why: Scheduled-vs-actual update fire time. Backlog here is exactly the 'stale data' symptom seen on Pixel 3 XL. p95 must stay near one 40ms frame.

injectionLagMaxMs.why: A single stall of 5+ frames is a visible freeze of a driving instrument, even if p95 looks fine.

updateToPaintP95Ms.why: Handler start to next painted frame. Data may arrive on time but pixels lag; 100ms keeps the display within ~2.5 frames of reality.

longestTaskMs.why: One long task blocks every queued update behind it. Applies after warm-up only.

heapGrowthMb.why: Growth over a 60s run. A leak that passes 60s but dies at 20 minutes of real driving shows up here as steady growth.

warmupMs.why: Initial layout, font loading, and JIT warm-up legitimately spike; steady-state driving is what gets gated. Load time is reported, not gated.

cpuThrottle.why: CDP CPU throttle factor approximating a Pixel 3 XL-class device on a CI runner. Calibrated in the rollout task; adjust this single number if too lenient/harsh.

defaultDurationMs.why: Default run length for local and CI checks. Long enough to surface sustained lag and heap growth without making every run drag on.

defaultRuns.why: Single run keeps CI feedback fast; re-run the job manually if a one-off outlier fails.

contractTimeoutMs.why: Fail quickly when an app never defines window.onCarStateUpdate instead of waiting for the full scenario duration.

contractPollMs.why: How often the shim checks whether the app has registered window.onCarStateUpdate after page load.

resultTimeoutPaddingMs.why: Extra time to let a run flush final browser work before the harness treats it as hung.

resultTimeoutMultiplier.why: Multiply the scenario duration by this much before treating the run as hung. Keeps a throttled but healthy app from timing out mid-run.

viewport.why: Landscape dashboard viewport on phone-class hardware. The apps render sideways in-car, so CI should not benchmark a portrait phone page.
